old: An estimated 10 to 12 million enslaved Africans were shipped across the Atlantic from the 1500s to the 1800s. Probably no more than a few hundred thousand were taken before 1600; demand rose sharply with Caribbean sugar in the 1600s, and roughly half of the trade took place in the 1700s.
new: An estimated 10 to 12 million enslaved Africans were shipped across the Atlantic from the 1500s to the 1800s. Probably no more than a few hundred thousand were taken before 1600; demand rose sharply with Caribbean sugar in the 1600s, and nearly three-fifths of the trade took place in the 1700s.
why: Britannica: "nearly three-fifths of the total volume of the transatlantic slave trade took place" in the 18th century, not roughly half.
